record.paper_title: (Two) Open Questions in Stellar Nuclear Physics
record.context_brief: S34(0) precision for the 4He(3He,γ)7Be solar-model reaction
record.original_question: How can the astrophysical cross-section factor S34(0) for the 4He(3He,γ)7Be reaction be measured with the high precision needed for the Standard Solar Model, given that it remains poorly known with a 9% error and must be improved before direct detection of 7Be solar neutrinos and high-precision prediction of all solar neutrino fluxes?

evidence.quote: reaction cross sections that must be measured with an accuracy of 5% or better are the 7Be(p, γ)8B reaction and the 4He(3He,γ)7Be reaction and the corresponding S17(0) and S34(0) defined in Ref. [8].

In contrast to the intensive work onS17(0), no progress what-so-ever was achieved on measuring S34(0) with high precision, and it is still poorly known with an error of 9% [8]. This inadequate situation must be improved in the near future as we expect the direct detection of 7Be solar neutrinos.
When the controversy on the composition of sun (Z/X) will also be resolved [13], it will allow high precision prediction of all solar neutrino fluxes including the 8B neutrino flux.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the radiative capture reaction $^{4}\mathrm{He}(^{3}\mathrm{He},\gamma)^{7}\mathrm{Be}$, which is a key branch in the proton–proton chain that fuels stars such as the Sun and produces $^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ (and subsequently $^{8}\mathrm{B}$) solar neutrinos. For a non-resonant charged-particle reaction with center-of-mass energy $E$, cross section $\sigma(E)$, and Sommerfeld parameter $\eta(E)$, the astrophysical S-factor is defined by
$$S(E)=E\,\sigma(E)\,\exp(2\pi\eta(E)),$$
and $S_{34}(0)$ denotes the zero-energy extrapolation of $S(E)$ for the $^{4}\mathrm{He}(^{3}\mathrm{He},\gamma)^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ reaction. The Standard Solar Model requires $S_{34}(0)$ to be known to an accuracy of 5% or better in order to enable precision predictions of the $^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ and $^{8}\mathrm{B}$ solar neutrino fluxes; at the time the question was posed, $S_{34}(0)$ was known only to about 9%, with a long-standing $\sim 3\sigma$ discrepancy between determinations based on prompt $\gamma$-ray detection and those based on $^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ activity measurements.

Problem: Devise an experimental and/or theoretical program that determines $S_{34}(0)$ for the $^{4}\mathrm{He}(^{3}\mathrm{He},\gamma)^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ reaction with a total (statistical plus systematic) uncertainty of 5% or less, and resolves the discrepancy between the prompt-$\gamma$ and activation methods.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made since the question was posed. LUNA underground measurements (e.g., Confortola et al. 2007) and the ERNA recoil-separator experiments produced new high-precision determinations of S34(0) using both prompt-gamma and activation methods, reconciling the previous discrepancy and yielding values near 0.56 keV·b with ~4–5% total uncertainty. Recent ab initio and effective field theory calculations (2024–2025) further refine the value. Thus the original 9% precision goal has effectively been reached for the 5% target, although community-recommended uncertainty quotations still hover at the 4–6% level and refinements continue.

status_evidence.title: Astrophysical S-factor of the 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be reaction measured at low energy via prompt and delayed gamma detection
status_evidence.snippet: High-precision LUNA measurement obtaining consistent S34(0) from prompt and activation methods.
status_evidence.claim: Modern underground experiments reduced the S34(0) uncertainty substantially and resolved the prompt-vs-activation discrepancy.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of 3He(alpha,gamma)7Be with ERNA Recoil Separator
status_evidence.snippet: ERNA recoil-separator determination of S34(0) complementing LUNA results.
status_evidence.claim: Independent recoil-separator measurement supports the new precision value of S34(0).

status_evidence.title: Precision calculation of 3He(α,γ)7Be for solar physics
status_evidence.snippet: Bayesian NNLO analysis yielding S34(0) ≈ 0.56 keV·b with refined uncertainty.
status_evidence.claim: Recent theoretical work continues to refine S34(0) to the few-percent level.
